notes.title: The Talos ban
notes.text: Talos, the deified Tiber Septim, was a Nord and is beloved in Skyrim, but the White-Gold Concordat outlawed his worship. Thalmor Justiciars hunt anyone keeping his shrines, so many Nords pray in secret, while Windhelm worships openly. Defying the ban divides the civil war.

notes.title: The Nine Divines
notes.text: The Empire's official faith honors the Eight Divines: Akatosh, Arkay, Dibella, Julianos, Kynareth, Mara, Stendarr and Zenithar. The ninth, Talos, has been officially struck out under the Concordat, though most Nords still count him.

notes.title: Akatosh
notes.text: Akatosh, the Dragon God of Time, is the chief of the Divines. Legend says he grants the Dragonborn their dragon souls, and the Nords sometimes link him with Alduin, though most priests reject that idea.

notes.title: Arkay
notes.text: Arkay is the god of birth, death and the cycle of life. His priests tend the Halls of the Dead in each city and see necromancy and the undead as abominations.

notes.title: Dibella
notes.text: Dibella is the goddess of beauty, love and art. Her greatest temple in Skyrim is in Markarth, served by priestesses who keep a young girl, the Sybil, as the goddess's living voice.

notes.title: Kynareth / Kyne
notes.text: Kynareth, whom Nords call Kyne, is the goddess of the sky, wind and nature; Nords say she gave men the power of the Voice. Her temple in Whiterun tends the Gildergreen, a sapling of the ancient Eldergleam tree.

notes.title: Mara
notes.text: Mara is the mother goddess of love and compassion. Couples in Skyrim marry at her temple in Riften, where Maramal will perform the ceremony for anyone wearing an Amulet of Mara who finds a willing partner.

notes.title: Stendarr
notes.text: Stendarr is the god of mercy, justice and righteous might. His Vigilants hunt Daedra worshippers and undead in his name.

notes.title: Julianos and Zenithar
notes.text: Julianos is the god of wisdom, logic and law, honored by scholars and magistrates. Zenithar is the god of work and commerce, favored by merchants and craftsmen.

notes.title: The old Nord gods
notes.text: Nords keep older names for many gods: Shor, the fallen god who rules Sovngarde; Kyne, the warrior widow of the sky; and Tsun, who guards the bridge into Sovngarde. Talos is also called Ysmir, the Dragon of the North.

notes.title: The Daedric Princes
notes.text: The Daedric Princes are powerful immortal beings who rule realms in Oblivion and meddle in mortal affairs, granting artifacts to those who serve them. Most respectable people in Skyrim see Daedra worship as dangerous or wicked, though Dunmer revere Azura, Boethiah and Mephala.

notes.title: Azura
notes.text: Azura is the Daedric Prince of dusk and dawn, revered by many Dunmer as a protector. A giant statue of her stands on a mountain south of Winterhold, carved by refugees from Morrowind, where a priestess named Aranea keeps watch.

notes.title: Molag Bal
notes.text: Molag Bal is the Daedric Prince of domination and enslavement, whose realm is Coldharbour. Legend says he created the first vampire, and his name is a curse in Skyrim.

notes.title: Hircine
notes.text: Hircine is the Daedric Prince of the hunt, father of werewolves and other beast-folk. His followers see life as a great chase, and the souls of werewolves are said to run forever in his Hunting Grounds.

notes.title: Sheogorath and Sanguine
notes.text: Sheogorath is the Mad God, Prince of madness, whose realm is the Shivering Isles. Sanguine is the Prince of debauchery and revelry, known for showing up at drinking contests with strange wagers.

notes.title: Nocturnal
notes.text: Nocturnal is the Daedric Prince of night, darkness and luck. Thieves pray to 'Lady Luck', and the Thieves Guild's fortunes are said to rise and fall with her favor.

notes.title: Malacath
notes.text: Malacath is the Daedric Prince of outcasts, sworn oaths and curses, and the patron god of the Orcs, who live by his Code in their strongholds. Nords know him as Mauloch, the orc-god their ancestors once fought.

notes.title: Mehrunes Dagon
notes.text: Mehrunes Dagon is the Daedric Prince of destruction and revolution. His invasion of Tamriel through the Oblivion gates two centuries ago is remembered as the Oblivion Crisis, and the Mythic Dawn cult that served him is supposed to be long gone.

notes.title: Vaermina, Namira and Boethiah
notes.text: Vaermina is the Daedric Prince of dreams and nightmares, Namira the Lady of Decay worshipped by secret cannibal cults, and Boethiah the Prince of deceit and conspiracy, whose cultists prize betrayal. All three are spoken of in Skyrim with fear and disgust.

notes.title: Meridia, Peryite, Clavicus Vile and Mephala
notes.text: Meridia is the Daedric Prince of life and light who despises the undead. Peryite rules pestilence, Clavicus Vile grants wishes with a catch through his talking dog Barbas, and Mephala, the Webspinner, deals in secrets, lies and murder.

notes.title: Hermaeus Mora
notes.text: Hermaeus Mora is the Daedric Prince of forbidden knowledge and fate, whose realm Apocrypha is an endless library. Scholars who seek his Black Books are said to be lost to madness or to his service.

notes.title: Sithis and the Night Mother
notes.text: Sithis is the Dread Father, the primal void and chaos that the Dark Brotherhood worships. The Night Mother is his spirit bride, who speaks only to a chosen Listener and passes on the prayers of those who perform the Black Sacrament.

notes.title: The Old Gods of the Reach
notes.text: The Forsworn and many Reachmen worship the Old Gods, which outsiders say are simply the Daedric Princes under other names. Their hagravens, witches transformed into half-bird crones, make briarhearts: warriors whose hearts are replaced by a magical briar.
